findings.evidence: `.github/workflows/pr-build.yml:24-25` triggers on `[opened, synchronize, reopened]`, while `push_ledger` queries all `pull_request_target` runs without their event action and `analyse_pr` treats every resulting epoch as a push.
findings.fix: Record the triggering event/action and accept only genuine head transitions (`opened` for the initial head and `synchronize` thereafter); reconstruct open/closed intervals so time outside the PR queue is not counted.
findings.issue: Every `opened` or `reopened` workflow run is treated as a pushed head, although reopening does not change the head; a repeated SHA can therefore become a new epoch and be reported at lines 457-461 as a resolving “push,” attributed to the user who reopened it.

findings.evidence: Lines 600-603 overwrite/store one row per SHA globally, and `ledger_index` at lines 315-317 can consequently assign that SHA only to the owner/branch from its earliest occurrence.
findings.fix: Preserve workflow runs as occurrence records keyed by PR or owner/branch plus timestamp/action, and deduplicate reruns using run/event identity rather than SHA.
findings.issue: The ledger is keyed only by commit SHA and retains the earliest run, conflating reruns with legitimate occurrences of the same SHA on another branch/PR or after a reopen; later transitions and their actor/time/branch are discarded.

summary: The workflow-run history is not a faithful push ledger: it includes non-push lifecycle events and collapses distinct head occurrences by SHA. This can fabricate resolutions, durations, and resolver attribution.
